newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber trade quiet, looks for direction.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber trade quiet, looks for direction.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Tuesday as people waited for leads from Japan and to see if any fresh buying emerges in the afternoon session, dealers said.
"The major consumers have pulled back again and we're basically waiting for leads this afternoon, especially from the Japanese market," a dealer said.

The morning session was fairly quiet a day after Michelin was said to have purchased several hundred tonnes of RSS3 rubber in the local market while other consumers were said to be sniffing around for prices, traders said.
The rubber trade was keeping an eye on the chance that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) may intervene in the market.
Traders said there was no impact in the market from the currency problems which have plagued the region.
"Business is quiet. Buying interest is a bit thin although this can quickly change later in the day," a dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 93.25 U.S. cents a kg from 94.25 cents. September RSS1 was indicated unchanged at 138.50 Singapore cents (96 U.S. cents) a kg.
